sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text:
Helsinki's recent policy works through resident parking, street prices and planning rather than bans. Resident parking has 16 zones with monthly permits at €45 to €64.50. The price in zone C is due to rise from €64.50 to €69.30 on 1 December 2026 [0]. On 24 March 2026 the City Environment Board decided, by 9 votes to 4, to extend resident and business parking to Käpylä, Kumpula, Toukola and Kulosaari, with other drivers limited to four hours on weekdays. Roll-out is planned for autumn 2026 or spring 2027 [1]. Street parking costs €4 an hour in the city centre and €2 in the inner city, on weekdays from 9:00 to 21:00 and Saturdays until 18:00 [2]. In August 2024 the city proposed that only fully electric cars keep the 50% street-parking discount from January 2025, but the page does not state the outcome [4].

Plans for the centre point the same way. The council approved the zoning change for Kaivokatu in front of the Central Station on 6 May 2026, though it is not yet legally binding. Construction is planned from 2028, and in a second phase, after the Esplanade streets are renovated in the early 2030s, Kaivokatu is planned to become a public-transport street [6]. A transport plan for Kluuvi and Kaartinkaupunki aims to increase the use of underground car parks and is studying a new service-tunnel link between them [8]. The city has also investigated an emission-free zone for the centre, but in November 2024 it was only under investigation [9]. In May 2025 the city proposed scrapping mandatory parking-space requirements for new housing in Pasila and south of Hakamäentie, and cutting them elsewhere [5].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text:
Most of what is changing is park-and-ride. City documents give average car park-and-ride utilisation of 83% in 2019 and 52% in 2021, with the most popular lots full and others half-empty. About 12% of users do not continue by public transport [12]. On 20 May 2025 the City Environment Board approved, as guidance, principles under which no car park-and-ride spaces are built into parking facilities in development projects in the core area, paid use is extended in stages, and users must identify as public-transport users at the busiest sites. It cites about 3,450 car spaces and 5,500 bicycle spaces [13]. Kulosaari's lot was announced to become paid from 23 November, at €1 for 12 hours with an HSL ticket or €1 an hour without [14]. The Redi car park, with 1,950 spaces, offers park-and-ride only on one floor on weekdays at €2 per 10 hours [16]. Fintraffic's LIIPI service has covered park-and-ride information nationally since May 2024 [15].

In the centre, Kamppi's two car parks hold 250 and 1,300 spaces [20], and Aimo Park's Finlandia garage has 650 spaces at €2 per half hour by day and €38 for 24 hours [19]. The Port of Helsinki is changing payment at its outdoor car parks: from 1 October 2026 the Aimo Park app ends and the Moovy app is introduced [17]. The tram to Laajasalo is scheduled to start on 7 November 2026 [11]. We found no sourced figures on a shift to shopping centres or on garage charging.

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
Our measured data for Helsinki are not downtown garages. They are 18 small lots from the Fintraffic park-and-ride feed, with 1,063 spaces in total and 17 to 141 spaces each, so they say little about the city centre. Fintraffic lists eight lots under FLS Finland, six under Kaupunkiliikenne Oy, two under EuroPark and two under Aimo Park. Most are listed with no hourly charge; Ruoholahti shopping centre is €3 an hour or €24 a day, and the Kulosaari and Ukko-Pekan lots charge €1 a day.

Occupancy over August to early October 2026 averaged 41% on weekdays and 21% at weekends, the pattern of commuter lots. The fullest are small lots: Rastila metro station (83% on weekdays, 42 spaces), Soittajantie (79%, 20 spaces), Jäkälätie (65%) and Siilitie east (62%, 17 spaces). The emptiest are Kulosaari (24%, 96 spaces), Vuosaari Mosaiikkiparkki (29%, 128) and Takkakuja (30%). The 141-space Ruoholahti shopping-centre car park is 39% full on weekdays and 5% at weekends. Only one lot, Ruoholahti, is within 2 km of Rautatientori. The data cover the summer holidays, so term-time figures may differ, and we have no multi-year history for Helsinki.
